statements: Configure deeper review for roles according to access and business risk
Surface specific signals and logs rather than a nationality or fraud verdict
Require multiple signals and a human determination
Retain auditable outcomes and trends while minimizing applicant data
Provide candidate notice, appeal, accessibility, and lawful data-retention controls
limitations: Signals require lawful, proportionate, accessible, privacy-preserving human review. Accent, ethnicity, nationality, visual similarity, camera behavior, geography, VPN use, remote work, or one device/network attribute must never act as a standalone detector.

statements: Ashby's product documentation illustrates a risk-based ATS workflow: customers select jobs for checks; the system considers device, IP, email, phone, location, identity, and assessment signals; reviewers see the underlying reasons; and humans mark outcomes rather than accepting an opaque fraud verdict.
limitations: These pages provide no DPRK-specific detection rate or validated performance evidence. Device and network attributes can create false positives for travelers, shared networks, accessibility tools, and privacy-protective users.
